findings.title: FeatureAgglomeration is registered as a hard clusterer but clusters FEATURES: wrong-length labels from cluster(), cryptic crash or silent 3-point plot from plot(), and a broken reuse path
findings.description: FeatureAgglomeration transposes the clustering problem (it groups columns, not rows), yet it sits in CLUSTERERS alongside KMeans and is documented in cluster()'s and plot()'s docstrings as a supported observation-clustering model. Four verified symptoms: (1) hyp.cluster(X_300x5, cluster='FeatureAgglomeration') returns 5 labels -- one per FEATURE -- while the docstring promises 'a list of cluster labels (one per observation)'; (2) hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster='FeatureAgglomeration') crashes with a cryptic sklearn error because default_params k=5 exceeds the 3 reduced columns; (3) hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster={'model': 'FeatureAgglomeration', 'n_clusters': 2}) runs without any warning and silently draws THREE points where the user's 300 observations should be (reshape_data regroups using the 3 per-feature labels) -- a wrong visualization with zero indication of data loss; (4) reusing a fitted FeatureAgglomeration Clusterer on the SAME data raises NotImplementedError whose message wrongly blames 'new data (a different number of rows than it was fit on)'. Either drop FeatureAgglomeration from the observation-clustering registry, special-case it, or document per-feature semantics everywhere.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
X = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 5)) + 8.0 * i for i in range(3)])
print(len(hyp.cluster(X, cluster='FeatureAgglomeration', n_clusters=3)))  # 5, not 300
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
hyp.plot(X[:, :4], '.', cluster={'model': 'FeatureAgglomeration', 'n_clusters': 2}, show=False)  # 3-point figure
hyp.plot(X[:, :4], '.', cluster='FeatureAgglomeration', show=False)  # ValueError
findings.expected: Per-observation labels (docstring: 'a list of cluster labels (one per observation)'), or a clear error/warning explaining FeatureAgglomeration clusters features
findings.actual: "FeatureAgglomeration": {"type": "list", "len": 5} on (300,5) input; plot dict k=2: 'total plotted points: 3 of 300 input rows; per-artist: [1, 2]' with no warning; plot default: 'ValueError: Cannot extract more clusters than samples: 5 clusters were given for a tree with 3 leaves.'; reuse on same data: 'NotImplementedError: FeatureAgglomeration has no out-of-sample prediction ... on new data (a different number of rows than it was fit on)'

findings.title: plot(cluster='DBSCAN'|'MeanShift'|'OPTICS'|'AffinityPropagation', n_clusters=k) crashes with a cryptic constructor TypeError; only HDBSCAN gets the friendly warn-and-ignore
findings.description: plot.py's cluster block special-cases ONLY HDBSCAN ('n_clusters is not a valid parameter for HDBSCAN clustering and will be ignored') and then unconditionally injects params['n_clusters'] = n_clusters for every other non-mixture model, so the four other density/bandwidth clusterers -- all listed as supported in plot()'s own docstring, right next to the documented n_clusters kwarg -- crash in the sklearn constructor. hyp.cluster() itself handles the same combination gracefully via its signature-based exemption (verified: cluster='DBSCAN', n_clusters=7 ignored). Fix: use the same inspect.signature check (or the shared _resolve_cluster_spec) in plot.

findings.title: plot(random_state=) is NOT threaded to the cluster stage, contradicting the docstring; seeded cluster plots are non-reproducible
findings.description: plot()'s random_state docstring says: 'Seed for reproducibility, threaded to the reduce/cluster stages: it is injected into any stage model whose constructor accepts a random_state (UMAP, TSNE, KMeans, GaussianMixture, ...)'. In code, random_state is passed only to analyze() (reduce/align path, plot.py ~line 1683); the two cluster-stage call sites -- clusterer(xform, cluster={'model': model, 'kwargs': params}) and clusterer(xform, cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=n_clusters) -- omit it, and default_params() contains no random_state. Verified: two identical hyp.plot(noise, '.', cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=6, random_state=0) calls produce different groupings. Scientists relying on the documented seeding for figures get silently irreproducible cluster colorings.
findings.repro:

import hypertools as hyp
noise = np.random.default_rng(3).standard_normal((120, 10))
f1 = hyp.plot(noise, '.', cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=6, random_state=0, show=False)
f2 = hyp.plot(noise, '.', cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=6, random_state=0, show=False)
# compare per-artist point sets -> differ
findings.expected: Identical cluster groupings across the two seeded calls (docstring: injected into KMeans/GaussianMixture etc.)
findings.actual: same groups across 2 seeded runs: False  -> plot(random_state=) NOT threaded to cluster= stage (docstring says it is)

findings.title: plot(cluster=..., return_model=True) without n_clusters: figure clusters with k=5 but the returned pipeline encodes k=3 -- the bundled 'exact fitted parameters' mismatch the figure
findings.description: The figure path resolves string cluster specs through _shared/params.py default_params (KMeans/Agglomerative/etc n_clusters=5; GaussianMixture n_components=5; LDA/NMF n_components=20), while the return_model bundle path pre-resolves the spec with _resolve_cluster_spec(cluster, n_clusters if n_clusters is not None else 3) -- i.e. cluster.cluster()'s default 3. Verified: hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster='KMeans', return_model=True) draws 5 groups (sizes [35, 32, 33, 100, 100]) while bundle['pipeline'].transform(data) yields 3 unique labels; for GaussianMixture the figure blends 5 components but the pipeline returns a (300, 3) proportions matrix. The bundle is documented as reusing 'these exact fitted parameters' on new data (plot.py return_model comment block and pipeline= docstring), so downstream analyses silently disagree with the published figure. Root cause is the divergent default k (see F13-cluster-021).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 4)) + 7 * i for i in range(3)])
res = hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster='KMeans', return_model=True, show=False)
print(len(set(map(int, res['pipeline'].transform(data)))))  # 3, but the figure shows 5 groups
findings.expected: The returned pipeline's cluster stage uses the SAME k the figure was drawn with (5, from default_params), so pipeline.transform reproduces the plotted grouping
findings.actual: figure groups (point-artists): 5 sizes: [35, 32, 33, 100, 100]; bundle pipeline labels unique k: 3 | GaussianMixture: bundle pipeline proportions shape: (300, 3) (figure used default_params n_components=5)

findings.title: Integer cluster labels passed as hue= render clusters 0 and 1 in visually identical reds -- the shipped plot_clusters2.py example produces a single-color plot
findings.description: The canonical documented workflow 'get cluster labels, then pass to hue to color points by cluster' (examples/plot_clusters2.py, tutorial cluster.ipynb hue=labels_10) is visually broken: numeric hue goes through the continuous multicolor path, and labels 0 and 1 map to (0.86, 0.34, 0.34) and (0.86, 0.371, 0.34) -- indistinguishable adjacent reds -- for EVERY k tested (2, 3, 4, 5, 10). With k=2 the whole plot is one red blob (verbatim run of the shipped example, and the weights/spiral workflows). The SAME labels converted to strings take the categorical path and render clearly distinct colors ((0.86, 0.371, 0.34) vs (0.34, 0.829, 0.86)). Not previously filed: F02-plot-hue covers other hue defects but not this label-0/1 collision. Fix likely belongs in the numeric-hue color normalization (mat2colors positioning); at minimum small-cardinality integer hues should use the categorical palette like strings do.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 3)), rng.standard_normal((100, 3)) + 3])
labels = hyp.cluster(data, n_clusters=2, random_state=0)
fig = hyp.plot(data, '.', hue=list(labels), show=False)
fc = [c for c in fig.axes[0].collections if getattr(c, '_offsets3d', None) is not None][0].get_facecolor()
print(sorted({tuple(np.round(x, 3)) for x in fc}))  # two near-identical reds
findings.expected: Visually distinct colors per cluster (the example's stated purpose: 'color our points by cluster'); string labels already behave this way
findings.actual: distinct colors: [(0.86, 0.34, 0.34, 1.0), (0.86, 0.371, 0.34, 1.0)] -- delta 0.031 in one channel; verbatim plot_clusters2.py output is a uniform red point cloud (see evidence)

findings.title: Reusing a fitted no-predict clusterer on DIFFERENT data with the SAME row count silently returns the stale fit-time labels
findings.description: Clusterer.transform's QC-2026-07 label-recovery fallback keys ONLY on row count: for hard clusterers without predict (AgglomerativeClustering, SpectralClustering, DBSCAN, OPTICS, HDBSCAN), any input whose row count equals the fit-time count gets the stored labels_ back, with no warning and no check that it is the same data. A scientist processing equal-sized sessions/batches (the norm in neuroimaging: same TR count per run) who reuses model from return_model=True on session 2 silently receives session 1's cluster labels as if they were fresh assignments. The docstring only says a fitted Clusterer 'is applied via .transform/.predict instead of being refit' -- nothing warns about this same-row-count aliasing. Suggest at minimum a UserWarning ('returning fit-time labels; X cannot be re-labeled without refitting'), or fingerprinting the fit data (shape+hash) before falling back.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
A = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((30, 4)) + 6 * i for i in range(2)])
labels_A, model = hyp.cluster(A, cluster='AgglomerativeClustering', n_clusters=2, return_model=True)
B = rng.standard_normal((60, 4)) * 50 + 100  # unrelated data, same row count
labels_B = hyp.cluster(B, cluster=model)
print(list(labels_B) == list(labels_A))  # True, silently
findings.expected: An error (like the different-row-count case) or an explicit warning that fit-time labels are being returned and B was never actually clustered
findings.actual: labels_B == labels_A (stale fit-time labels returned for unrelated data): True; any warning raised: none (silent)

findings.title: plot(cluster=False) raises ValueError although plot's docstring documents the type as 'str, dict, False, or None'
findings.description: plot()'s cluster docstring line reads 'cluster : str, dict, False, or None', but the code gates on `elif cluster is not None:` and then rejects anything that is not str/dict, so cluster=False crashes with 'Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!'. Either accept False as no-clustering (consistent with hyp.cluster(), where False is falsy-passthrough via the `if cluster is None` ... actually cluster=False currently passes through cluster()'s formatter path returning formatted data) or fix the docstring type line.
findings.expected: No clustering applied (documented False behaves like None), or a docstring that does not list False
findings.actual: ValueError: Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!

findings.title: Silent conflict resolution in cluster specs: an instance beats n_clusters= with no warning, and a dict carrying BOTH 'params' and 'kwargs' silently ignores 'params'
findings.description: (a) hyp.cluster(data, cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=5), n_clusters=3) returns 5 clusters -- the docstring says instances are 'used as-is' but nothing tells the user their explicit n_clusters=3 was discarded; a warning would prevent silent surprises. (b) cluster={'model': 'KMeans', 'params': {'n_clusters': 2}, 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 4}} yields k=4: the branch order checks 'args'/'kwargs' first so the legacy 'params' dict is dropped without the DeprecationWarning or any notice.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
data = np.random.default_rng(1).standard_normal((150, 4))
print(len(set(map(int, hyp.cluster(data, cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=5, random_state=0), n_clusters=3)))))  # 5, no warning
print(len(set(map(int, hyp.cluster(data, cluster={'model': 'KMeans', 'params': {'n_clusters': 2}, 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 4}})))))  # 4, no warning
findings.expected: A UserWarning naming the ignored setting in both cases
findings.actual: n_uniq: 5 (5 => instance wins silently) / dict with BOTH params and kwargs ... n_uniq: 4 (no warning emitted in either run)

findings.title: n_clusters precedence is inconsistent between hyp.cluster and hyp.plot: spec kwargs win in cluster(), explicit n_clusters= wins in plot()
findings.description: With cluster={'model': 'KMeans', 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 2}} plus n_clusters=4: hyp.cluster returns k=2 (model_params.setdefault('n_clusters', ...) preserves the spec) while hyp.plot draws k=4 groups (params['n_clusters'] = n_clusters overwrites the spec). The same spec produces different clusterings depending on which entry point runs it, so a figure and its accompanying cluster() analysis can silently disagree.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 4)) + 7 * i for i in range(3)])
spec = {'model': 'KMeans', 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 2, 'random_state': 0}}
print(len(set(map(int, hyp.cluster(data, cluster=spec, n_clusters=4)))))  # 2
fig = hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster=spec, n_clusters=4, show=False)  # 4 groups
findings.expected: One consistent precedence rule (and ideally a conflict warning) across cluster() and plot()
findings.actual: hyp.cluster -> k = 2 (kwargs wins) / hyp.plot -> figure groups = 4 (explicit n_clusters wins)

findings.title: plot cluster dict without a 'model' key raises a bare KeyError; hyp.cluster gives a helpful ValueError for the same input
findings.description: hyp.cluster({'kwargs': ...}) raises "ValueError: If passing a dictionary, pass the model as the value of the 'model' key and a dictionary of custom parameters as the value of the 'kwargs' key (the legacy 'params' key is also accepted)." -- excellent. plot() reads cluster['model'] directly (plot.py cluster block) and surfaces a raw KeyError: 'model' with no guidance.
findings.expected: The same instructive ValueError hyp.cluster raises
findings.actual: KeyError: 'model'

findings.title: Invalid instance specs fail with cryptic AttributeErrors: cluster=42 -> "'int' object has no attribute 'fit'"; an sklearn Pipeline fits fine then dies on '.labels_'
findings.description: Any non-str/class/dict spec is assumed to be a scikit-learn-style instance and used as-is. cluster=42 crashes with AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'fit'. Worse, a legitimate sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline ending in KMeans -- a natural thing to pass given the docstring's 'pass a scikit-learn style instance directly' -- successfully FITS and only then crashes with AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'labels_' (sklearn Pipelines do not proxy labels_). A type check with a clear message (and/or a fit_predict fallback, which sklearn Pipelines DO support) would fix both.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
X = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((60, 3))
hyp.cluster(X, cluster=42)  # AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'fit'
hyp.cluster(X, cluster=Pipeline([('s', StandardScaler()), ('k', KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=10))]))
findings.expected: A ValueError naming the accepted spec forms; ideally support fit_predict-only estimators such as sklearn Pipelines
findings.actual: RAISED AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'fit' / RAISED AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'labels_'

findings.title: List of datasets with mismatched column counts fails with a raw np.vstack error that never mentions datasets or columns
findings.description: hyp.cluster([ (50,4) array, (50,3) array ]) surfaces numpy's concatenation error verbatim. Scientists mixing recordings with different feature counts (a supported scenario elsewhere in hypertools, where reduce aligns dimensionality) get no hint that cluster() requires equal column counts or that reduce= first would fix it.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
hyp.cluster([rng.standard_normal((50, 4)), rng.standard_normal((50, 3))], n_clusters=2)
findings.expected: An error naming the mismatched datasets/column counts and suggesting reduce= (or padding) first
findings.actual: ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly, but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 4 and the array at index 1 has size 3

findings.title: cluster(..., normalize='zscore') raises AssertionError (wrong exception type) from the normalize stage; the manip vocabulary ('ZScore') is not accepted by normalize=
findings.description: Passing normalize='zscore' through cluster's cross-module kwarg hits tools/normalize.py line 242's assert, producing AssertionError: 'scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.' The message content is decent but (a) AssertionError is the wrong type for input validation (vanishes under python -O; callers catch ValueError), and (b) the confusion is natural since manip='ZScore' IS valid one kwarg over (verified working). Primary fix belongs to the normalize unit; filed here because it is reachable through cluster()'s documented cross-module kwargs.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((60, 4)) + 6 * i for i in range(3)])
hyp.cluster(data, normalize='zscore', n_clusters=5, random_state=0)
findings.expected: ValueError listing valid values (and ideally recognizing the near-miss 'zscore' -> "did you mean manip='ZScore' or normalize='across'?")
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: Every default HDBSCAN run emits sklearn's FutureWarning about the 'copy' parameter
findings.description: sklearn 1.8's HDBSCAN warns 'The default value of `copy` will change from False to True in 1.10. Explicitly set a value for `copy` to silence this warning.' on every fit when copy is unset. Since hypertools constructs the model, every hyp.cluster(x, cluster='HDBSCAN') and the HDBSCAN gallery example emit a warning the user did not cause and cannot cleanly silence through the simple string spec. Setting copy explicitly in the registry/default construction (behavior-neutral: pin copy=False or accept True) removes the noise.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((200, 5))
hyp.cluster(X, cluster='HDBSCAN')  # FutureWarning from sklearn
findings.expected: No warning on default use
findings.actual: sklearn/cluster/_hdbscan/hdbscan.py:722: FutureWarning: The default value of `copy` will change from False to True in 1.10. Explicitly set a value for `copy` to silence this warning.

findings.title: cluster() docstring omits the random_state parameter entirely
findings.description: cluster()'s signature has random_state=None (injected into any model accepting it -- verified working for KMeans/SpectralClustering/GaussianMixture), but the docstring's Parameters section documents x, cluster, n_clusters, return_model, manip/normalize/reduce/align, ndims and format_data only. Users cannot discover the reproducibility knob from help(hyp.cluster).
findings.repro: python -c "import hypertools; import inspect; print('random_state' in inspect.signature(hypertools.cluster).parameters, 'random_state :' in hypertools.cluster.__doc__)"
findings.expected: random_state documented like plot()'s docstring documents its own
findings.actual: Signature contains random_state=None; the docstring Parameters section (cluster.py lines 140-193) has no random_state entry

findings.title: plot() docstring lists LatentDirichletAllocation and NMF as supported cluster= values, but plot clusters the PCA-reduced (signed) scores so they crash even on non-negative input data
findings.description: plot() clusters xform -- the post-reduce scores -- and IncrementalPCA scores are essentially always signed, so cluster='LatentDirichletAllocation' or 'NMF' via plot raises 'Negative values in data passed to ...' regardless of the raw data (verified with all-non-negative input for NMF). hyp.cluster()'s docstring carries the note 'LatentDirichletAllocation and NMF require non-negative data' but plot()'s cluster docstring lists them with no caveat, and no hint that the reduction step is what breaks them.
findings.expected: Docstring caveat (or a targeted error explaining that clustering runs on reduced scores and suggesting hyp.cluster on the raw data instead)
findings.actual: ValueError: Negative values in data passed to NMF initialization. (and ...to LatentDirichletAllocation.fit. for LDA on standard data)

findings.title: Tutorial cluster.ipynb: false claim that n_clusters is specified for HDBSCAN, a 'HCBSCAN' title typo, and an incomplete supported-models list
findings.description: Three defects in docs/tutorials/cluster.ipynb: (1) cell 19 markdown says VERBATIM 'In this case, we specify both the clustering model (HDBSCAN) and the number of clusters (10).' while cell 20's code is labels_HDBSCAN = hyp.cluster(mushrooms, cluster='HDBSCAN') -- no n_clusters, and HDBSCAN takes none; (2) cell 21 titles the second figure 'HCBSCAN clustering' (typo); (3) cell 2 lists the supported models as 'MiniBatchKMeans, AgglomerativeClustering, Birch, FeatureAgglomeration, SpectralClustering and HDBSCAN', omitting MeanShift, DBSCAN, OPTICS, AffinityPropagation and all four mixture models that 1.0 supports. The tutorial's testable numeric claims verified fine (default mushrooms labels {0,1,2}; n_clusters=10 -> 10 unique labels).
findings.repro:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
nb = json.load(open('docs/tutorials/cluster.ipynb'))
for i in (2, 19, 20, 21):
    print(i, ''.join(nb['cells'][i]['source'])[:200])
EOF
findings.expected: Tutorial text matches its code and the 1.0 model registry; correct spelling
findings.actual: cell 19: 'we specify both the clustering model (HDBSCAN) and the number of clusters (10).'; cell 20: hyp.cluster(mushrooms, cluster='HDBSCAN'); cell 21: title='HCBSCAN clustering'; cell 2 model list omits 8 supported models

findings.title: Shipped gallery example plot_clusters3.py uses the deprecated legacy {'model','params'} spec and emits a DeprecationWarning when run
findings.description: examples/plot_clusters3.py passes cluster={'model':'HDBSCAN','params':{...}} -- the exact form 1.0 deprecates in favor of {'model','args','kwargs'} -- so building the gallery (and every user who copies the official example) triggers 'DeprecationWarning: {'model': ..., 'params': {...}} is deprecated'. The example text also instructs 'you will need the dictionary form which includes both the model and the params'. Should be updated to the canonical kwargs form.
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg python -W always::DeprecationWarning examples/plot_clusters3.py
findings.expected: Official examples demonstrate the canonical (non-deprecated) spec
findings.actual: WARN DeprecationWarning: {'model': ..., 'params': {...}} is deprecated; use {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} instead (verbatim run)

findings.title: README says 'cluster(ndims=...) arguments were removed' but cluster() still accepts ndims= -- and silently no-ops it unless reduce= is also given
findings.description: README.md ('Retired legacy arguments' bullet) states VERBATIM that the 'cluster(ndims=...)' argument was removed. The 1.0 signature still takes ndims=None, repurposed as a reduce-stage passthrough; the cross-module branch checks only (manip, normalize, reduce, align), so hyp.cluster(x, ndims=2) -- the 0.x idiom that used to reduce before clustering -- runs and silently ignores ndims with no warning. A migrating 0.x user gets different results with zero feedback. Either warn when ndims is given without reduce=, or align the README/docstring with the actual behavior.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((100, 10))
a = hyp.cluster(X, n_clusters=3, ndims=2, random_state=0)
b = hyp.cluster(X, n_clusters=3, random_state=0)
print(list(a) == list(b))  # True -- ndims silently ignored
findings.expected: A warning ('ndims= has no effect without reduce=') or README/docstring accuracy about the repurposed argument
findings.actual: cluster.py line 219 gates the pipeline path on (manip, normalize, reduce, align) only; ndims-only calls take the single-stage path unchanged. README.md: 'and `cluster(ndims=...)` arguments were removed.'

findings.title: plot(cluster=) accepts only str/dict while hyp.cluster accepts strings, bare classes, instances, and fitted Clusterers -- an API asymmetry
findings.description: hyp.cluster's spec grammar (string | class | instance | dict | fitted Clusterer) is documented and works. plot() rejects classes and instances with 'Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!'. Anyone graduating from hyp.cluster(data, cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=4)) to plot(data, cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=4)) hits a wall. plot's docstring does honestly document only str/dict (plus the broken False, F13-cluster-007), so this is inconsistency rather than doc breakage.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
hyp.plot(np.random.randn(60, 4), '.', cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=3, n_init=10), show=False)
findings.expected: plot accepts the same spec grammar as hyp.cluster (it could delegate to _resolve_cluster_spec)
findings.actual: ValueError: Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!

findings.title: Divergent default k: hyp.cluster defaults n_clusters=3, plot's cluster='KMeans' defaults to 5 via _shared/params.py (and LDA/NMF to 20) -- none of it documented
findings.description: hyp.cluster(x) yields 3 clusters; hyp.plot(x, cluster='KMeans') draws 5 groups (default_params: KMeans/MiniBatchKMeans/Spectral/Agglomerative/FeatureAgglomeration/Birch n_clusters=5, GaussianMixture/BayesianGaussianMixture n_components=5, LDA/NMF n_components=20). plot's n_clusters docstring does not state any default, so the 3-vs-5 divergence is invisible until it bites -- and it directly causes the return_model bundle mismatch (F13-cluster-004). One shared default (or documenting both) would remove the surprise.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 4)) + 7 * i for i in range(3)])
print(len(set(map(int, hyp.cluster(data)))))  # 3
fig = hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster='KMeans', show=False)  # 5 groups
findings.expected: Same default k across entry points, or explicit documentation of each default
findings.actual: hyp.cluster default -> 3 unique labels; plot(cluster='KMeans') -> n point-artists (groups): 5

findings.title: Cluster legend entries are unsorted label strings (['1', '0', '2'])
findings.description: plot(data, '.', cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=3, legend=True) produces legend entries in first-appearance order ('1', '0', '2') rather than sorted ('0', '1', '2'), which reads as sloppy in publication figures and makes cross-figure comparison harder. Labels are bare integers with no 'cluster' prefix either.
